previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis, coronary artery disease, and a history of prior stents presented with severe substernal chest pain radiating to the right arm, occurring at rest and relieved partially by nitroglycerin. Initial evaluation revealed a mildly elevated troponin, consistent with unstable angina. He underwent cardiac catheterization, which showed in-stent restenosis in the mid-distal right coronary artery, and successfully received a drug-eluting stent. During the hospitalization, he experienced transient hyperkalemia corrected with dialysis and had a self-limited episode of guaiac-positive dark stools with a transient drop in hemoglobin, managed with pantoprazole. His blood pressure was managed with adjustment of isosorbide mononitrate. He remained stable, completed scheduled dialysis, and was discharged home on dual antiplatelet therapy, optimized cardiac medications, and instructions for outpatient follow-up including endoscopy and cardiology evaluation.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ year old gentleman with a history of ESRD on dialysis ___ 
at ___) who presents with a two day history of bilateral leg 
pain and hematuria, with ED course notable for fever.  

# Fever: The etiology is most consistent with a viral syndome 
given his URI symptoms, body aches, and cough. He is 
reassuringly flu negative. Pneumonia unlikely with clear cxr and 
absence of wbc elevation. Dysuria/hematuria could point to 
cystitis, though absence of pyuria on UA makes this unlikely. 
Bacteremia in the setting of HD also possible but blood cultures 
negative x2. No GI sx and negative LFTs. No HA to suggest 
meningitis. No e/o septic hip joint on exam. His systolic 
ejection murmur has been documented in the past, and although 
nonspecific body aches are often presenting symptoms of 
endocarditis, this appears less likely in the context of viral 
symptoms. Never received antibiotics, viral panel negative. 
Improved with supportive care.

# Bilateral leg pain: Acute on chronic in the setting of fevers 
may be arthralgias superimposed on OA, discharged with short 
course of oxycodone and attempted to arrange with outpatient 
pain management. He was given a short course of oxycodone to 
bridge to PCP follow up. 

# ESRD on HD MWF: ___ glomerulonephritis, failed RUE AVF, has 
working left upper extrem AVF. He missed his HD day of admission 
and presented with K of 6.7 in the ED. He was seen by renal in 
the ED and received dialysis prior to admission, K normalized. 
 
# Hypoglycemia: Likely secondary to insulin he received in the 
ED for hyperkalemia vs poor PO intake. He is s/p 2 amps D50 in 
the ED with blood sugars in 100's. 

# Hematuria: UA notable for trace blood. No evidence of UTI. 
History of hematuria dating to ___ on review of OMR labs. 
Differential includes necrosis or injury to transplanted kidney, 
though renal team unconerned about further workup. He is 
scheduled for close followup with urology for repeat UA and 
possible cystoscopy. 

TRANSITIONAL ISSUES:
# Urology follow up scheduled for hematuria workup
# Pain management to be arranged by PCP, patient given phone 
number for pain clinic, short course of oxycodone to bridge to 
PCP appt

radiology_notes.text:
EXAMINATION:  BILAT HIPS (AP,LAT AND AP PELVIS)

INDICATION:  History: ___ with hip pain  // eval osteonecrosis      eval
osteonecrosis

TECHNIQUE:  Single AP view the pelvis and two views of each hip.

COMPARISON:  Pelvis radiographs from ___

FINDINGS: 

There is abnormal mixed lucency and sclerosis at bilateral femoral heads
compatible with previously noted avascular necrosis. There is increased
lucency and collapse of the superior articular surface of the right femoral
head compared with previous study. There is mild bilateral hip joint
degenerative change. There is dense vascular calcification, and the right
common iliac artery appears aneurysmal measuring 1.7 cm.

IMPRESSION: 

Known avascular necrosis with interval progression of right-sided femoral head
cortical collapse.

INDICATION:  End-stage renal disease on hemodialysis presenting with cough and
shortness of breath. Evaluate for edema or infiltration.

TECHNIQUE:  Frontal and lateral views of the chest.

COMPARISON:  Chest radiograph ___ and ___. Chest CT ___.

FINDINGS: 

The lungs are mildly hyperinflated, as evidenced by flattening of the
diaphragms on the lateral view. Diffuse interstitial markings, compatible with
known chronic interstitial lung disease, are unchanged.  There is no pleural
effusion or evidence of pulmonary edema. There is no focal airspace
consolidation worrisome for pneumonia. Mild to moderate cardiomegaly is
unchanged. The mediastinal and hilar contours are unremarkable. A coronary
artery stent is noted.  There is a levoscoliosis of the thoracic spine.

IMPRESSION: 

Stable changes of chronic interstitial lung disease without evidence of a
superimposed acute cardiopulmonary process.
